# Part 1 · Sub-Ångstrom 3D Resolution {.divider}

> Simulation reaches 10⁸ atoms. **Can measurement follow — atom by atom, in 3D?**

<div class="roadmap r3">
<div class="rtile active"><img src="./media/extracted_media/02_ptychography.png"><div class="rlbl">1 · Sub-Ångstrom 3D</div></div>
<div class="rtile"><img src="./figs_imc21/tiles/gdox_ffstem.gif"><div class="rlbl">2 · Fused FF-STEM</div></div>
<div class="rtile"><video src="./figs_imc21/vortex/frft_vortex_linkedin_crop.mp4" autoplay muted loop playsinline></video><div class="rlbl">3 · Transverse state</div></div>
</div>

## Ptychographic tomography: put the scattering physics in the model

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](./media/images/4dstem_tomo.mp4){controls="true" autoplay="true" data-autoplay="true" muted="true" loop="true" height="780px"}
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
Depth information is encoded in the **illumination angles** — for large convergence angles, a single scan already carries 3D information.

![](./media/images/MultisliceAlgorithm.mp4){controls="true" autoplay="true" data-autoplay="true" muted="true" loop="true" width="640px"}

Forward model — multislice, paraxial, time-independent:
$$\mathcal{M}_{\psi}(\mathbf{V}) = \prod_{k=0}^T (\mathcal{P}^{\Delta z} T^{\mathbf{V}_k})\psi$$
:::
:::

::: {.callout-note}
Atomic 3D resolution from a 4D-STEM tilt series — with multiple scattering modelled explicitly, not approximated away
:::

## First unknown 3D atomic structure solved by phase-contrast tomography

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="46%"}
1. 4D-STEM tilt series
2. mixed-state ptychography at every tilt
3. joint linear tomography and alignment
4. sub-pixel atomic peak tracing
5. 3D atomic-structure determination

![](./media/extracted_media/image67.png){width="88%"}
:::
::: {.column width="54%"}
![Volume size: (6 nm)³](./media/extracted_media/media1_clip.mp4){controls="true" autoplay="true" data-autoplay="true" muted="true" loop="true" width="72%"}
:::
:::

::: {.callout-note .fragment}
Elliptic double-wall CNT resolved in 3D; a **novel ZrTe₂ phase**, confirmed stable by DFT
:::

::: aside
@Pelz_2023
:::

## End-to-end reconstruction alleviates the missing wedge

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
Fully end-to-end MSPT differentiates through the *whole* chain — affine resampling of the volume, z-resampling, batch-cropping, mixed-state multislice, far-field propagation, and gradient backpropagation through all of it.

![](./media/extracted_media/image88.png){height="520px"}
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![Light *and* heavy atoms recovered over a 90° tilt range](./media/extracted_media/image127.png){height="620px"}
:::
:::

::: {.callout-note .fragment}
Physical priors recover the missing wedge → near-isotropic 3D resolution (Nyquist 0.82 Å), at **12× virtual sub-sampling**
:::

::: aside
@Romanov_2024, @You_Romanov_Pelz_2024
:::

## The payoff: atomic resolution in all three directions

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](./media/extracted_media/media24_sq.mp4){width="83%" controls="true" autoplay="true" data-autoplay="true" muted="true" loop="true"}

# Chemistry, and the cost of scale {.divider}

> Ptychography delivers weak chemical contrast. **Spectroscopic STEM provides complementary contrast. Existing forward models however are expensive and do not scale well.**

## Core-loss EELS maps cannot be read off directly

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- Atomic-resolution **EELS elemental maps are not projections**: the focused probe undergoes strong **dynamical scattering**
- Quantitative interpretation needs full quantum-mechanical simulation of the probe *before* **and** *after* the core-loss transition
- So the forward model becomes the bottleneck for **inversion**
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![Simultaneous five-edge atomic-resolution maps across a LaAlO₃/SrTiO₃ interface](./media/figs_aachen/lao_sto_hero.png){width="100%"}
:::
:::

::: {.callout-note .fragment}
Core-loss chemistry is the richest — and one of the more expensive — signals to simulate
:::

::: aside
@pelz2026bipprismalgorithmfastscalable
:::

## Bi-partitioned PRISM-EELS: and it scales

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="42%"}
![Probe leg ($\mathcal{S}_1$) and detector leg ($\mathcal{S}_2$), each on a **sparse set of parent beams**, reconstructed on a small window at the ionized atom](./media/figs_aachen/method_schematic.png){width="100%"}

**Bi-partition both** scattering matrices → the per-scan exit propagation **disappears**
:::
::: {.column width="58%"}
<div class="scaling-figure-grid" role="group" aria-label="Scaling benchmarks versus thickness, grid size, and scan count">
<img src="./media/figs_aachen/map_scaling_panel_a.png" alt="Map compute time versus specimen thickness">
<img src="./media/figs_aachen/map_scaling_panel_b.png" alt="Peak GPU memory versus simulation grid size">
<img src="./media/figs_aachen/map_scaling_panel_c.png" alt="Map compute time versus number of scan positions">
</div>
:::
:::

::: {.callout-note .fragment}
LaAlO₃/SrTiO₃, **five core-loss edges at once**, 32 041 probe positions: **~89 s, 2.4 GB** on one GPU — **>50×** lower memory
:::

::: aside
@pelz2026bipprismalgorithmfastscalable

Building on Ophus 2017, Brown 2019, Pelz 2021
:::

# Part 2 · Fused Full-Field STEM {.divider}

> One scan already illuminates several detectors. **Why throw any of them away?**

<div class="roadmap r3">
<div class="rtile"><img src="./media/extracted_media/02_ptychography.png"><div class="rlbl">1 · Sub-Ångstrom 3D</div></div>
<div class="rtile active"><img src="./figs_imc21/tiles/gdox_ffstem.gif"><div class="rlbl">2 · Fused FF-STEM</div></div>
<div class="rtile"><video src="./figs_imc21/vortex/frft_vortex_linkedin_crop.mp4" autoplay muted loop playsinline></video><div class="rlbl">3 · Transverse state</div></div>
</div>

## Sensor fusion: gap-free contrast in near-real time

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="62%"}
![Fused Full-Field STEM (FF-STEM) on Gd₂O₃ nanohelices](./media/figs_aachen/fusion_fig1.png){width="100%"}
:::
::: {.column width="38%"}
- **Direct ptychography** → coherent **high-frequency phase**
- **Tilt-corrected dark-field** → **low-frequency** amplitude contrast
- fused in Fourier space by Wiener-type weighting with **SSNR-based weights**
:::
:::

::: {.callout-note .fragment}
Closes the low↔high spatial-frequency gap → one **aberration-free** image. Analytic, non-iterative: **< 1 s** on a single GPU.
:::

::: aside
@You_2026
:::

## Fusion works on real, low-dose data

::: {layout="[[1]]"}
![Experimental FF-STEM vs. parallax across detectors: AuNPs and Gd₂O₃ nanohelices (Timepix4, 1211 e⁻/Å²)](./media/figs_aachen/fusion_fig4.png){fig-align="center" width="80%"}
:::

::: {.callout-note .fragment style="margin-top: 40px;"}
Robust across samples and detectors
:::

::: aside
@You_2026
:::

# Part 3 · Transverse Quantum State Characterization {.divider}

> Many structured-illumination proposals assume a coherent state.
> **What transverse quantum state does a programmable MEMS phase plate actually deliver?**

<div class="roadmap r3">
<div class="rtile"><img src="./media/extracted_media/02_ptychography.png"><div class="rlbl">1 · Sub-Ångstrom 3D</div></div>
<div class="rtile"><img src="./figs_imc21/tiles/gdox_ffstem.gif"><div class="rlbl">2 · Fused FF-STEM</div></div>
<div class="rtile active"><video src="./figs_imc21/vortex/frft_vortex_linkedin_crop.mp4" autoplay muted loop playsinline></video><div class="rlbl">3 · Transverse state</div></div>
</div>

## Motivation: a wealth of proposals for programmable electron optics




## Mixed-state ptychography measures the whole illumination

![Dominant probe mode in the aperture plane, ℓ = −17 … +17. Hue = phase, brightness = amplitude. The winding number is directly countable; the dark wedge is the needle-band shadow.](./figs_imc21/vortex/mode_gallery_fourier.png){width="100%"}

::: {.callout-note .fragment}
21 charge states, from **standard 4D-STEM** using ptychography<br>
Two stages: BF-disk shift estimation with a vortex ramp, then a **mixed-state** iterative solver.
:::

::: aside
MEMS device: CNR Modena (V. Grillo). @you2026transversequantumstatecharacterizationprogrammable
:::

## The device is linear and calibratable

From the OAM spectrum of the reconstructed probe density matrix:
$$\langle \ell \rangle = \sum_\ell \ell\, P_\ell, \qquad P_\ell = \rho_{\ell\ell}$$

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](./figs_imc21/vortex/sorter_mean_l_vs_bias.png){width="90%"}
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](./figs_imc21/vortex/sorter_voltage_calib.png){width="95%"}
:::
:::

::: {.callout-note .fragment}
**16.8 ħ per applied volt** across ℓ = −17 … +17.<br>
programmed charge maps onto the delivered charge by stable gain 
:::

::: aside
@you2026transversequantumstatecharacterizationprogrammable
:::

## But the delivered beam is not one wave

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="56%"}
![](./figs_imc21/vortex/mode_stack.png){width="100%"}
:::
::: {.column width="44%"}
![](./figs_imc21/vortex/purity_vs_l.png){width="100%"}
:::
:::

::: {.callout-note .fragment}
At ℓ = +17 the dominant mode carries only **42 %** of the power. Purity falls and entropy rises: the higher the charge you program, the more mixed the beam you get.
:::

::: aside
@you2026transversequantumstatecharacterizationprogrammable
:::

## Partial coherence, measured in both planes

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="62%"}
![Aperture-plane coherence envelope \|γ(Δk)\|](./figs_imc21/vortex/coherence_fourier.png){width="100%"}
:::
::: {.column width="38%"}
![](./figs_imc21/vortex/coherence_widths.png){width="100%"}
:::
:::

::: {.callout-note .fragment}
The aperture-plane coherence width **collapses by ~3×** from ℓ = 0 to \|ℓ\| = 17, while the real-space envelope stays near the source-size limit — the mixedness lives in the *aperture*, exactly where a vortex phase plate acts.
:::

::: aside
@you2026transversequantumstatecharacterizationprogrammable
:::

## Dose budget to reach given resolution

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="58%"}
![](./figs_imc21/vortex/dose_to_snr5.png){width="100%"}
:::
::: {.column width="42%"}
![](./figs_imc21/vortex/dose_efficiency_vs_l.png){width="100%"}
:::
:::

- We derive a **generalized weak-phase SSNR for mixed probes**: $\Gamma_\rho(q,k) = J(k-q,k) - J(k,k+q)$, giving $\mathrm{SSNR}_\rho = \sqrt{2L_{\mathrm{up}}}\,D_{\mathrm{coh}}$. → DQE → partial coherence-aware dose budget

::: {.callout-note .fragment}
**Dose rule:** below $q \approx 0.5\,q_{\mathrm{probe}}$ the vortex is the cheaper probe; above it, pay for purity or use a round aperture.
:::

::: aside
@you2026transversequantumstatecharacterizationprogrammable

Reduces to Nellist–Rodenburg, Bennemann and Varnavides in the appropriate limits
:::

## Summary 

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="66%"}
- **Sub-Ångstrom 3D** — ptychographic electron tomography reaches sub-Ångström, near-isotropic 3D *beyond* the depth-of-focus limit
- **core-loss EELS simulations at scale** [@pelz2026bipprismalgorithmfastscalable] — BiP-PRISM allows core-loss EELS + 4D-STEM **past one million atoms** on one GPU
- **FF-STEM** [@You_2026] — Wiener sensor fusion gives gap-free, aberration-free contrast in **< 1 s**, robust at low dose
- **Transverse quantum state characterization** [@you2026transversequantumstatecharacterizationprogrammable] — mixed-state ptychography can now be used to characterize the transverse quantum state of a programmable MEMS phase plate



:::
::: {.column width="33%"}
